title: Former Peak Resorts owners buying Wyoming's Snowy Range
h1: The Boyd family, who sold Peak Resorts to Vail in 2019, is buying Wyoming's small Snowy Range ski area
description: The Boyd brothers and Brendan Ryan, who ran Peak Resorts before its 2019 sale to Vail, are buying Snowy Range near Laramie, the Colorado Sun said Nov. 16.
standfirst: The family that sold 17 ski areas to Vail Resorts is getting back into the business with a 250-acre hill west of Laramie. The buyers say it is a long-term family investment, and the price was not disclosed.
keywords: Snowy Range ski area sale, Boyd family Snowy Range, Peak Resorts Vail 2019, Laramie ski area, Wyoming ski resort sale, Jesse Boyd
takeaways: Jesse, Jason and Joshua Boyd and partner Brendan Ryan are buying Snowy Range Ski Area from the Maddox family; the price was not disclosed.
The group ran Peak Resorts, which Vail Resorts bought in 2019 for $11 a share, a deal The Colorado Sun valued at $264 million.
Snowy Range, about 30 miles west of Laramie, lists a December 4, 2026 to April 11, 2027 season and adult season passes from $349.
body: Three brothers whose family built Peak Resorts, a 17-area ski company that Vail Resorts bought in 2019, are buying the Snowy Range Ski Area in southern Wyoming, The Colorado Sun reported on November 16. Jesse, Jason and Joshua Boyd are buying the hill with their friend Brendan Ryan, another former Peak executive. The seller is the Maddox family, which has owned it since 2010. The price was not disclosed.

The ski area sits about 30 miles west of Laramie in the Medicine Bow National Forest. Its website lists 250 skiable acres. The Sun put the hill at four lifts and 27 trails, while the resort's site lists five lifts and 30 trails. Adult tickets bought at the window run $59 on non-peak days, and adult season passes start at $349, according to the site. By comparison, the Sun noted, walk-up day tickets at big destination resorts top $390 this winter.

The Maddoxes bought the area from a bank in 2010 with investors, after a 2003 fire had destroyed the lodge. The Sun said they more than tripled visitation and revenue in their first decade, and that this was the first offer the family had received in years.

Tim Boyd opened a single lift at Hidden Valley near St. Louis in 1982, and Peak Resorts grew into a chain of ski areas stretching from Missouri to New Hampshire that went public in 2014. Vail paid $11 a share in 2019 and added the 17 areas to its Epic Pass. Jesse Boyd, Peak's former chief operating officer, told the Sun the Snowy Range deal is meant to keep the families in skiing for the long haul.
The resort's website lists the 2026-27 season as December 4 through April 11. The Sun did not report a closing date for the sale.
